chunks: "Standing at Arafah is a sunnah (prophetic tradition), and at al-Mash'ar is an obligation, and whatever else of the rites is sunnah (prophetic tradition)."

key_terms.الْمَنَاسِكِ: The ritual acts and rites of hajj
key_terms.الْوُقُوفُ: Standing or remaining at the designated sacred site during hajj rites
key_terms.بِالْمَشْعَرِ: At al-Mash'ar, the sacred site of Muzdalifah during hajj
key_terms.بِعَرَفَةَ: At Arafah, the well-known place of standing during hajj
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: A prescribed prophetic practice, here indicating a non-obligatory rite
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ: An obligation that is legally required

ai.seo_question: Which rites of hajj are obligatory and which are sunnah according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between levels of obligation within the rites of hajj. It states that standing at al-Mash'ar is obligatory, while standing at Arafah and the other rites are described as sunnah (prophetic tradition), highlighting a legal hierarchy in the manasik.
